native_mechanisms: The bone-colored die-stone never resets between marks: state is carried forward so every fold inherits the accumulated effect of all prior folds (single sequentially-dependent accumulator).

Each mark's weight is pressed into the stone's already-turned position, not a clean face, so early marks bend how later marks land, and a one-bit difference is multiplied forward each fold until no two paths converge (order-dependent, avalanching mixing step).

Only the stone's final seated position read against the fixed wooden keeps ever leaves the desk; all intermediate turns and residue are discarded (final-state-only output with fixed constants, no intermediate emission).
core_technique: Verbatim xxHash64 (4-lane add/multiply/rotate/multiply accumulator with length-tagged tail and xor-shift-multiply avalanche finalizer) plus an AVX2 XXH3 long-input path (8 accumulator lanes, secret-keyed mul_epu32 accumulate, periodic scramble, mul128-fold merge) — i.e. the known multiply-xor-shift accumulator approach, with the native's "never resets" and "final seat only" amounting to restatements of what any such accumulator already does, and the parallel 4/8 lanes actually contradicting the single-stone sequential chain.
